newsitem.title: FINLAND: FOCUS - Metsa-Serla Q1 pft plunges.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Metsa-Serla Q1 pft plunges.

text.p: Finnish forest industry group Metsa-Serla Oy on Monday reported first quarter earnings down 46 percent on the year-ago period, but said it saw improving profitability in the second half.

Metsa-Serla -- Finland's third largest forestry group -- said first quarter profit after financial items fell to 129 million markka ($25.5 million) from 239 million in the year-ago period, while earnings per share dropped to 0.22 markka from 1.15 markka.

"The fall in profit is due to the fact that prices for almost all products, but particularly for market pulp and coated magazine paper, were considerably lower than last year," Metsa-Serla said in a statement.
But Metsa-Serla said it expected a better second half.
It expected "favourable profitability development during the second half of 1997, providing the positive market development continues."

The profit was well above analysts' median forecast for a profit before extraordinary items and tax of 20 million markka, but it was within the unusually broad range of forecasts which went from a loss of 50 million to a profit of 170 million.
At 1340/1040 GMT, Metsa-Serla's B share traded up 0.50 markka at 40.00, off a session low of 39.00 markka, in fair nine million markka volume.
Group net sales rose to 3.93 billion markka in January-March from 3.75 billion a year ago, while the operating profit fell to 288 million from 393 million markka, Metsa-Serla said.
Operating profit was down to 7.3 percent of turnover, from 10.5 percent a year ago, it said.
Prices of coated magazine paper fell during the first quarter and were more than 20 percent lower than in the same quarter of 1996, but delivery volumes rose on last year.
"The market for magazine papers is now improving, and both prices and profitability are expected to be better during the second quarter," it said.

Prices of coated fine paper fell almost 10 percent and prices of uncoated fine paper by more than 10 percent, but demand for fine papers remained strong and delivery volumes surpassed those of the same period last year, it said.
But demand for fine papers was expected to slacken, at least temporarily, in the second quarter, Metsa-Serla said.
Sales volume and profitability had improved considerably at its Swiss Biberist fine paper mill, acquired at the turn of the year.
Demand for tissue paper was steady in the Nordic region, but grew two to three percent elsewhere in Europe, and sales volumes were steady, it said.
Softwood pulp prices fell during the second quarter to $520 per tonne from $560 per tonne in the same period last year, Metsa-Serla said.
Metsa-Serla said market pulp producers had cut production at the start of the second quarter so stocks would fall and prices rise before the summer.
But it warned that "if (pulp) prices are successfully increased, the latter part of the year might see growth in production and oversupply."
